title: How to suggest edits in Google Docs on Mac: step by step in your browser
metaTitle: How to Suggest Edits in Google Docs on Mac (2026 Steps)
description: Learn how to suggest edits in Google Docs on Mac: switch to Suggesting, select text, type, and explain changes. Steps checked November 2026.
targetKeyword: how to suggest edits in google docs on mac
secondaryKeywords: google docs suggest edits keyboard shortcut
intro: To suggest edits in Google Docs on Mac, open the document, switch the mode dropdown at the top right to Suggesting, then select text and type. Your changes appear in a new color with deletions crossed out, and the file owner decides whether to keep each one.
tldr: You need Commenter or Editor access. With View access, click Request edit access and ask the owner to share the file with you.
Click the mode dropdown at the top right, choose Suggesting, or press ⌘⌥⇧X before you type.
Select text, type your change, and watch it appear in a new color with deletions crossed out.
Click a suggestion, type a comment, and click Reply to explain why you changed it.
The owner reviews with Tools > Review suggested edits, then clicks Accept or Reject.

blocks.text: Suggesting is how you propose changes to someone else's Google Doc without changing the text itself. Your edits show up as marked changes. The owner can keep each one or reject it. This matters when you review a draft for a manager, a client, or a co-author who wants to see your reasoning first.

Google Docs runs in a browser tab on your Mac, so every step below happens in the browser. Google's help pages for suggesting do not give version numbers, and they do not name a browser. These steps reflect Google's help as of November 7, 2026. If a label looks slightly different on your screen, look for the same idea: a mode switch at the top right, a Suggest edits button in the margin, and a comment box.
Check that you can suggest before you start

Suggesting needs Commenter or Editor access to the file. A Viewer role lets you read the document, but it does not let you propose changes. Confirm your role before you spend an hour on edits. A quick message to the owner can save a wasted afternoon.

items: Commenter: you can leave comments and suggest changes.
Editor: you can change text directly and also suggest changes.
Viewer: you can read the document, but you cannot suggest.
No access: click Request edit access, and the owner can share the file with you.

blocks.text: If you cannot suggest, Google's help says to click Request edit access. The owner then shares the file with you as a Commenter or Editor. Pick Commenter if you only plan to leave notes and small fixes. Editor gives more power, so ask for it only when the work calls for direct changes.
What your suggestion looks like on screen

Once you type, your new words appear in a color that stands apart from the owner's text. Deletions are crossed out instead of vanishing. Google's help describes this directly. The owner sees the original and your change in one view, without any extra tool.

The live text does not change until the owner accepts the suggestion. This is the main reason to use suggesting. You can propose a rewrite of a paragraph, and the author still decides what the final version says. Treat each suggestion as a question, not a finished edit.

Try a small change first. Make a copy with File > Make a copy, then practice on that copy. Select one word, switch to Suggesting, and change it. Check that the change appears in a new color before you attempt a larger edit. A practice run takes a minute and shows you the layout.
How to explain a suggestion so the owner can decide

A bare change can confuse the owner. They see the new words but not your reason. Add a short comment to every suggestion that changes meaning. Click the suggestion, type your comment, and click Reply. The owner gets an email and decides whether to keep each suggestion.

items: Name the problem first: 'The claim needs a source.'
Then name the fix: 'Shorter to fit the word limit.'
Keep each comment to one reason, so the owner can answer it fast.
Save style debates for a separate conversation, not the margin.

blocks.text: Comments also help when you make the same kind of change many times. Explain it once in a comment, then point back to that thread in later comments. The owner reads faster, and you avoid repeating the same reason beside every edit.
Review suggested edits as the document owner

If you own the document, you decide what stays. Open Tools > Review suggested edits. A box appears at the top right. Click the Down arrow to preview the document with or without the changes. Then choose Accept all or Reject all.

You can also work through suggestions one at a time. Click a comment on the suggestion, then choose Accept or Reject. Click Comments at the top right to see the full list. Work from the top of the document down, so each decision follows the one before it.

rows: Hold Ctrl+⌘, press O, then U
Hold Ctrl+⌘, press N, then U
blocks.caption: Mac shortcuts from Google's keyboard shortcut page

blocks.text: Keyboard shortcuts for suggesting on Mac
The fastest way into suggesting is ⌘⌥⇧X. Hold Command, Option, and Shift together, then press X. To go back to direct editing, press ⌘⌥⇧Z. To view the document without any marks, press ⌘⌥⇧C.

Google lists no shortcut for accepting or rejecting a suggestion. Use the Tools menu or the comment buttons instead. Google also says some shortcuts may not work for every language or keyboard, so test them on your setup before you rely on them. Some third-party sites list other Mac keys, such as ⌘⌥⇧I. Use the keys on Google's own page.
Mistakes that make suggestions hard to review

items: Typing while Editing is on. Your words become direct changes with no marks. Check the dropdown before you type.
Rewriting a whole paragraph at once. Select the exact sentence instead, so the owner sees what moved.
Leaving a rewrite with no comment. The owner then has to guess why the change matters.
Mixing unrelated fixes into one suggestion. Split them, so each one can be accepted or rejected alone.
Forgetting that the owner gets an email for each suggestion. Expect a stream of notices after a long review.

blocks.text: Watch for shared drafts where several people suggest at the same time. Overlapping edits make the review slower. Agree on one reviewer per section when you can, and tell the others which section is theirs.
Suggesting in Word and other file formats

Many teams pass drafts between Google Docs and Microsoft Word. Google's help says that when you convert files to or from Microsoft Office, tracked changes and suggestions are converted. Open the converted file and scroll through the marked changes before you send it on.

Look for your comments in the converted file too. Google's note names tracked changes and suggestions, and it does not mention comments, so check them yourself. Keep the original Google Doc as a backup until you have confirmed the converted file looks right.
Suggesting offline in Chrome or Edge

Google's offline help covers Chrome and Edge. Offline access needs the Google Docs Offline extension, installed and turned on. Edge users are sent to the Chrome Web Store to get it. Google's page does not say whether suggesting works offline, so test that before a flight or a train ride.

Only one Google account per browser profile can have offline access. If you use a work account and a personal account, give each one its own profile. Very large files can fail to sync, so Google's help suggests splitting them into smaller documents.
Next steps after your first suggestion

After the owner answers, click Comments at the top right and read the replies. If you want to build more Docs skills on Mac, read [how to add a header and footer in Google Docs](/how-to/add-a-header-and-footer-in-google-docs). For dictating into a document, see [how to use voice typing in Google Docs](/how-to/use-voice-typing-in-google-docs).
If you write for a living, the [Google Docs guide for writers on Mac](/for/writers/google-docs) covers shortcuts, templates, and offline editing in one place.

faq.question: Do I need a Google account to suggest edits?
faq.answer: In practice, yes. Suggesting needs Commenter or Editor access on the file. If you cannot suggest, Google's help says to click Request edit access, and the owner shares the file with you in one of those roles.

faq.question: Why can I not see the Suggest edits button?
faq.answer: Select the text first, because the button appears in the right margin after you select. If it still does not appear, check your access level. View-only access cannot suggest, so ask the owner for Commenter or Editor access.

faq.question: Can I suggest edits in Safari on Mac?
faq.answer: Google's suggesting page does not name a browser. Its offline page lists Chrome and Edge, not Safari. This page did not verify Safari, so if the steps do not match what you see, switch to Chrome for this task.

faq.question: How do I accept every suggestion at once?
faq.answer: Open Tools > Review suggested edits, then click the Down arrow to preview. Click Accept all to keep every suggestion, or Reject all to remove them. Read the preview before you choose, because the choice applies to the whole document.

faq.question: What happens to suggestions when I convert the doc to Word?
faq.answer: Google's help says tracked changes and suggestions are converted when you convert files to or from Microsoft Office. Open the Word file and check the marked changes before you send it on, and look for your comments too.

faq.question: Can I switch back to direct editing after I suggest?
faq.answer: Yes. Press ⌘⌥⇧Z to switch to Editing, or open the mode dropdown at the top right and choose Editing. Changes you type after that are direct edits, not suggestions.

faq.question: Can I suggest edits without an internet connection?
faq.answer: Google's offline help covers Chrome and Edge, and it needs the Google Docs Offline extension. The page does not say whether suggesting works offline, so test it before you travel.

task: Suggest edits in a Google Doc on Mac
appliesTo: Google Docs in a browser on macOS, with Commenter or Editor access to the file
requirements: A Google account with Commenter or Editor access to the document
Google Docs open in a browser on your Mac
Owner access if you need to accept or reject suggestions

steps.name: Confirm you can suggest
steps.text: Open the Google Doc in your browser. Check your access before you type. You need Commenter or Editor access. If you only see View access, click Request edit access and wait for the owner to share the file with you.

steps.name: Switch the mode to Suggesting
steps.text: Look at the top right of the Google Docs window. Click the mode dropdown, which may say Editing. Choose Suggesting from the list. You can also press ⌘⌥⇧X. Your next changes become suggestions, not direct edits.
steps.tip: Check the dropdown before you type. If you forget, your words change the text directly.

steps.name: Select the text you want to change
steps.text: Drag across the words, or double-click a single word. Once the text is selected, a Suggest edits button appears in the right margin. Select one idea at a time so each suggestion stays easy to review.

steps.name: Type your change
steps.text: Type the new words, or press Delete to remove the selected text. Your change appears in a new color. Deleted words stay visible and crossed out, so the owner can see what you removed.
steps.tip: Keep each suggestion small. Small changes are easier to accept or reject.

steps.name: Explain the change in a comment
steps.text: Click the suggestion you made. Type a short reason in the comment box. Click Reply to post it. Google's help says the owner gets an email and decides whether to keep each suggestion.
steps.tip: Name the problem first, then the fix.

steps.name: Wait for the owner to decide
steps.text: Repeat the selection, typing, and comment steps for each change. The owner decides whether to keep each suggestion, one at a time or in a batch. You do not need to do anything else after that.

steps.name: Review suggestions as the owner
steps.shortcut: Hold Ctrl+⌘, press O, then U
steps.text: Owners open Tools > Review suggested edits from the menu. A box appears at the top right. Click the Down arrow to preview the document with or without the changes. Then click Accept all or Reject all.
steps.tip: To go through one suggestion at a time, click its comment and choose Accept or Reject.

shortcuts.keys: Hold Ctrl+⌘, press O, then U
Hold Ctrl+⌘, press N, then U
Hold Ctrl+⌘, press P, then U

troubleshooting.problem: The Suggest edits button does not appear
troubleshooting.fix: Select the text again, since the button shows after a selection. Then check your access. Commenter or Editor access is required. If you are a Viewer, click Request edit access.

troubleshooting.problem: My typing changed the text directly with no marks
troubleshooting.fix: The mode was on Editing. Press ⌘Z to undo the direct change, switch to Suggesting with ⌘⌥⇧X or the top right dropdown, then retype the change.
Google says some shortcuts may not work for every language or keyboard. Use the dropdown and the menus instead. Ignore shortcuts from third-party sites that differ from Google's page.

troubleshooting.problem: Another user has already enabled offline access on this computer
troubleshooting.fix: Google allows only one account per browser profile for offline access. Create a separate Chrome profile for the second account.
Check your network connection first. Very large files may fail to sync, so split the document into smaller files and try again.
